summary.text: Cristian Morales is the Republican candidate in California's 43rd District. Born in Guatemala, he describes a 20-plus-year career in manufacturing leadership, most recently as a director of operations. He ran for California governor in 2022 (a first campaign for office) and is running now on a campaign slogan of "ForAllVoices," according to his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.

paragraphs.text: Morales was born in Guatemala City, Guatemala, and, according to his Candidate Connection survey, his family immigrated to the United States during the 1970s.

He graduated from West Lafayette High School in Indiana, according to Ballotpedia, and earned a bachelor's degree in management from Purdue University in 2002, a graduate degree from Indiana University in 2007, and a graduate degree in industrial and labor relations from Cornell University in 2008.

Morales describes a career of more than 20 years in manufacturing, in the automotive, aerospace and defense sectors, leading multicultural teams; Ballotpedia lists his profession as business executive and his career as a director of operations.

He ran as a Republican for California governor in 2022, describing it as his first venture into politics; he received 25,086 votes in the June top-two primary and did not advance to the general election.
He advanced from the June 2, 2026 primary to the November general election for the 43rd District, which his survey says includes Compton, Watts, Hawthorne, Inglewood, Gardena, Lawndale and Torrance.
